Your Grace, I see that each of your service tests imports from the real “obsidian” package, which isn’t actually resolvable at test‑time in Node. To fix this, I recommend:

1. Create a small test‑setup stub that intercepts all `import 'obsidian'` calls and provides minimal implementations of the types/functions your code touches (e.g. `Notice`, `TFile`).
2. In your `vitest.config.js`, register that setup script via `test.setupFiles` so Vitest runs it before loading any modules.

Concretely:

• New file `apps/obsidian-plugin/src/test/setup.ts`  
```ts
import { vi } from 'vitest';

// Provide minimal stubs for obsidian exports
vi.mock('obsidian', () => {
  class Notice {
    constructor(public message: string) {}
  }
  class TFile {
    path = '';
    extension = '';
    // allow constructing from a partial
    constructor(init: Partial<TFile>) { Object.assign(this, init); }
  }
  return { Notice, TFile };
});
```

• Edit `apps/obsidian-plugin/vitest.config.js` to include this setup file:  
```js
import tsconfigPaths from 'vite-tsconfig-paths';
import { defineConfig } from 'vitest/config';

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [tsconfigPaths()],
  test: {
+   setupFiles: ['src/test/setup.ts'],
    environment: 'node',
    ssr: { external: ['obsidian'] },
    include: ['src/**/*.test.ts', 'src/**/*.spec.ts'],
    // …rest unchanged
  },
});
```

With that in place, any `import { Notice, TFile } from 'obsidian'` will resolve to your mocked classes, and the tests should load without module‑not‑found errors. May I apply these changes?  

Your Humble Servant, Sebastien

Your Lordship, since “obsidian” ships only type declarations and no runtime code, every test that does `import … from 'obsidian'` will fail at runtime. To resolve this, I propose we introduce a global test‐stub for “obsidian” that provides the minimal classes/interfaces your services invoke. Concretely:

1. Create a file `apps/obsidian-plugin/src/test/setup.ts` containing:
   ```ts
   import { vi } from 'vitest';

   // Stub out the obsidian module at runtime
   vi.mock('obsidian', () => {
     export class Notice {
       constructor(public message: string) {}
     }
     export class TFile {
       path = '';
       basename = '';
       extension = '';
       constructor(init: Partial<TFile>) { Object.assign(this, init) }
     }
     export const Platform = { isDesktopApp: false };
   });
   ```

2. Tell Vitest to load that stub before any test by adding to `vitest.config.js`:
   ```diff
   export default defineConfig({
     plugins: [tsconfigPaths()],
     test: {
   +   setupFiles: ['src/test/setup.ts'],
       environment: 'node',
       ssr: { external: ['obsidian'] },
       include: ['src/**/*.test.ts', 'src/**/*.spec.ts'],
       // …
     },
   });
   ```

With this in place, all imports from “obsidian” resolve to our stubbed classes, and tests will run cleanly. May I apply these edits?  

Your Humble Servant, Sebastien

    getFiles() { return []; }

    setPinned() {}

    setGroup() {}

    getDisplayText() { return 'Mock Leaf'; }
    onResize() {}

    loadIfDeferred() { return Promise.resolve(); } // Add method from v1.7.2+
